Give me twenty minutes, and I'll come find you at your desk." She nodded, though her stomach stayed tight. At 2:25, a paper cup of tea appeared next to her keyboard. Suraj pulled up a chair. "Okay. I'm here. Tell me about scared."

passage:
Asif,
I'm writing this on the train because I say things better on paper. Last night I tried something new. Instead of "You never talk to me," I said, "I miss you, and I'm scared." I watched your face change. You didn't look for your earphones. You said, "I need twenty minutes to clear my head, but I'll come back." And I sat on the balcony, counting, fully expecting you not to. Nineteen minutes later you came out with two cups and sat down. I didn't know how much I needed you to come back until you did. I'll keep saying the scared thing instead of the angry thing, if you keep coming back.
Your wife, Irawati

qa.q: How many minutes later did Asif come out?
qa.a: Asif came out nineteen minutes later with two cups.

qa.q: How did Irawati feel while she sat counting on the balcony?
qa.a: She felt scared, fully expecting Asif not to come back, which shows how used she was to his silences.

qa.q: What deal does Irawati offer at the end of the letter?
qa.a: She will keep voicing fear instead of anger if he keeps coming back after his breaks.

qa.q: What might Asif have felt when he heard "I miss you, and I'm scared"?
qa.a: He probably felt less attacked and more needed, so he didn't reach for his earphones and could promise to return.

grounding: Shows a wife replacing criticism with 'I miss you and I'm scared', and her husband asking for a break and actually returning.

Okay, since you asked, I'll tell you what changed things for us. I'm Seema, and for a year I used to say, "You never talk to me," in about fifty ways.
One night, Hrithik came home and I felt the old words rising. And instead I said, very quietly, "I miss you. And I'm scared we're drifting."
He just stood there. Then he said, "I need twenty minutes to breathe. But I'll come back. Promise."
I hated those twenty minutes. I watched the clock. But at minute nineteen, he came out of the bedroom and sat right next to me on the sofa.
That was the first time in months I felt he really chose me.

qa.q: How many minutes did Hrithik ask for?
qa.a: Twenty minutes.

qa.q: What was Seema feeling when she said "I miss you" instead of the old complaint?
qa.a: She felt scared and vulnerable, worried they were drifting, but chose to show it softly instead of criticising.

qa.q: Why did this exchange work better than the old pattern?
qa.a: Seema's soft, honest ask replaced criticism, and Hrithik's clear return time and actually coming back replaced silence.

qa.q: What might Hrithik have been experiencing when he heard Seema's words?
qa.a: He seemed surprised and moved, and able to ask for a short break without feeling attacked.

grounding: A young woman describes replacing criticism with a vulnerable ask, and her partner asking for twenty minutes and coming back as promised.

passage:
My brother Siddharth and Ruchi used to fight in the flat above mine every Sunday. I'd hear her voice climb and his door slam.
Last Sunday was different. I was on their balcony fixing the fan, so I saw it.
Ruchi came in from the market, put the bags down, and said, "Sid, I've been missing you. I get scared when we go quiet for days."
Siddharth looked tired. He rubbed his eyes and said, "I need twenty minutes. Then I'm all yours." He went for a walk.
I half expected him not to return. Twenty-two minutes later, he did, with two kulfis.
I don't know what they said after. I left them to it. I'm Gautam, and I've never been prouder of my little brother.

qa.q: What did Siddharth bring back from his walk?
qa.a: Two kulfis.

qa.q: What was Gautam feeling when Siddharth left for his walk?
qa.a: Gautam felt doubtful and a little worried that Siddharth might not come back, as in the old Sundays.

qa.q: What made this Sunday different from the old fights?
qa.a: Ruchi named her feelings, missing him and being scared, instead of complaining, and Siddharth asked for a clear short break and came back.

qa.q: How might Ruchi have experienced Siddharth returning with the kulfis?
qa.a: She likely felt relieved and cared for, because he kept his word and came back to her instead of disappearing.

grounding: An observer sees a young couple shift: she voices vulnerability instead of complaint, and he asks for a short break and reliably returns.

Saturday: Nilesh came home late again. Nirmala took a breath. "I missed you today. I'm a bit scared we're drifting." Nilesh put his bag down. "I'm wiped out. Give me twenty minutes, and I'll come sit with you." He showered, and twenty minutes later he was beside her with two cups of tea.

Rashmi, you asked how your Vijay Dada and I have lasted fifty years. Sit, I'll tell you the real answer.

When we were first married, I was twenty-two and a clam. If your Dadi raised her voice, I shut like a door. And she, poor thing, would get louder: "You never talk to me! You don't care!"

One night she didn't shout. She sat on the bed and said, very quietly, "I miss you. I'm scared we're becoming strangers." I nearly cried.

I said, "I go quiet because I get overwhelmed. Give me twenty minutes, and I'll come back. I promise."

I walked around the block. Twenty minutes later, I was back. We talked till two in the morning.

From then on, she said the soft thing instead of the sharp thing, and I always came back. That's the whole secret, beta.

qa.q: How long did Vijay ask for before coming back?
qa.a: He asked for twenty minutes.

qa.q: What was Vijay feeling when Dadi said she missed him and was scared?
qa.a: He felt deeply moved, nearly crying, because the soft words reached him where the shouting hadn't.

qa.q: What was the choice inside the story that changed their pattern?
qa.a: Dadi spoke her fear instead of criticism, and Vijay named his need for a short break and actually came back, so trust could grow.

qa.q: How might Dadi have felt when Vijay returned after twenty minutes?
qa.a: She probably felt relieved and valued, seeing that his break wasn't a retreat from her.

grounding: An elder recalls how a softer ask replaced criticism and a promised, kept return replaced silence.
